bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation and a recent acute coronary syndrome or PCI treated with a P2Y12 inhibitor, apixaban resulted in less ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than a vitamin K antagonist (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.81).
implications: Based on the reported 6-month outcomes, apixaban (vs vitamin K antagonist) was associated with a lower incidence of ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (10.5% vs. 14.7%; hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.81) and a lower incidence of death or hospitalization (23.5% vs. 27.4%; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.93), while the composite of death or ischemic events was not significantly different (hazard ratio, 0.93; 0.75–1.16). Aspirin (vs placebo) increased ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (16.1% vs. 9.0%; hazard ratio, 1.89; 1.59–2.24), while death or hospitalization was not significantly different (hazard ratio, 1.08; 0.96–1.21) and death or ischemic events was not tested for superiority after a nonsignificant hierarchical result.
